Hi Jane — great questions, thanks for sending them over. High level answers below; I can follow up with a short summary doc and a Marketplace URL.

- Billing/invoicing: Marketplace purchases are billed through AWS and you'll receive a consolidated AWS invoice. Direct contracts are invoiced directly by Redwood (monthly or net-30 custom terms). If your finance team prefers a single vendor invoice, Marketplace often wins.

- Tax & PO: AWS handles tax collection depending on region; PO acceptance flows are via AWS procurement. For direct deals we accept POs and can support custom tax handling on our invoices.

- SLA & data residency: Our SLA and data residency commitments are available for both purchase routes, but certain contractual security exhibits (e.g., bespoke audit language or CFT redlines) are easier to accommodate in a direct contract.

- Pricing & co-sell: Pricing is typically equivalent on-list, but Marketplace sometimes has platform fees. For strategic deals we can offer co-sell incentives and SOW/commit discounts via an enterprise contract that are generally not available through standard Marketplace SKUs — however, AWS co-sell may offer credits or incentives on some deals; I loop Rajiv from AWS to confirm what AWS can offer for ACME.

Next steps: I'll put together a one-page comparison and an M.A.P. (mutual action plan) for the team. Do you have any internal procurement deadlines or a target PO date?

Thanks,
